narration: Welcome to the module on the Sitz Bath Procedure, prepared by Bodhi Learning Labs.
Comfort and hygiene are essential parts of quality nursing care, particularly for patients in pain, swollen or uncomfortable in the perineal area.

A sitz bath is a simple but highly effective nursing intervention. It relieves pain, improves circulation, promotes healing and helps the patient relax after childbirth, surgery or an anorectal condition.
In this first section you will learn what a sitz bath is, when it is indicated, when it must not be used, the three types, and the temperature, duration and frequency that make it safe and effective.

narration: A sitz bath is a simple, safe and effective intervention, used across a range of perineal and anorectal conditions.
It is indicated for hemorrhoids, episiotomy wounds, postpartum perineal pain, anal fissure, rectal surgery, perianal abscess, and discomfort following urinary catheterisation.
Each of these is a different problem, and the sitz bath helps each one in a slightly different way. Let us take them in two groups.

slides.dev_notes: All seven reveal as one group on the second narration line - this slide is the overview; each condition is narrated in detail on the two that follow.

reveal.text:
Hemorrhoids — Swollen veins around the rectum.
Warm water relaxes the muscles, improves circulation and reduces inflammation.
reveal.cue_narration_line: Hemorrhoids are swollen veins around the rectal area, causing severe pain, itching, swelling and discomfort, especially during bowel movements. A warm sitz bath relaxes the muscles, improves blood circulation, reduces inflammation and soothes the area.

reveal.text:
Anal fissure — A small tear in the anal lining.
The bath relaxes the sphincter, reduces spasm and speeds healing.
reveal.cue_narration_line: An anal fissure is a small tear in the lining of the anus, causing intense pain and bleeding on defecation. The sitz bath relaxes the anal sphincter, reduces spasm, relieves pain and promotes faster healing of the fissure.

reveal.text:
Rectal surgery — Pain, swelling and irritation after the procedure.
The bath keeps the area hygienic and supports wound healing.
reveal.cue_narration_line: Patients who undergo surgery involving the rectum or anal area may have pain, swelling and irritation afterwards. A sitz bath is commonly advised to maintain hygiene, reduce discomfort and support wound healing during recovery.

reveal.text:
Perianal abscess — Pus collecting near the anus.
The bath improves drainage and reduces inflammation.
reveal.cue_narration_line: In a perianal abscess, pus collects near the anus causing swelling, redness and pain. A sitz bath helps improve drainage, reduce inflammation and relieve discomfort.

reveal.text: Contraindication / precaution | Why it matters | What the nurse does
reveal.cue_narration_line: Before performing a sitz bath, it is very important to understand its contraindications and precautions, to ensure patient safety and prevent complications.

reveal.text: Active bleeding | Warm water increases circulation and can worsen bleeding from the perineal or rectal area | Avoid, or proceed only on medical advice
reveal.cue_narration_line: A sitz bath should be avoided, or performed only with caution, in patients with active or excessive bleeding from the perineal or rectal area, because warm water may increase circulation and worsen the bleeding.

reveal.text: Severe infection or deep wounds | Improper technique can spread infection or damage tissue | Seek medical evaluation before the procedure
reveal.cue_narration_line: Patients with severe infection, extensive tissue damage or deep wounds may require medical evaluation before the procedure, as improper technique can spread infection.

reveal.text: Unconscious or uncooperative patient | The patient cannot report discomfort - risk of falls, burns and injury | Do not perform; the procedure needs cooperation
reveal.cue_narration_line: A sitz bath needs the patient's cooperation and their ability to communicate discomfort. Unconscious, confused or uncooperative patients are at higher risk of falls, burns and injury.

reveal.text: Allergy to medicated solution | Antiseptic or medicated additives can cause irritation, redness or an allergic reaction | Check allergies before adding any solution
reveal.cue_narration_line: If any antiseptic or medicated solution is to be added to the water, check for allergies first, to avoid skin irritation, redness or an allergic reaction.

reveal.text: Impaired sensation or neuropathy | A diabetic or neuropathic patient may not feel excessive heat | Assess temperature yourself; do not rely on the patient
reveal.cue_narration_line: Patients with impaired sensation or neuropathy - diabetic patients in particular - may not feel excessive heat. These patients are at greater risk of burns and skin damage, so extra caution and careful temperature assessment are necessary.

reveal.text: Very hot water | Causes burns and tissue injury | Check the temperature every time, before the patient sits
reveal.cue_narration_line: And excessively hot water is itself a major risk. It causes burns, tissue injury and discomfort, so always check the water temperature before starting.

narration: Before performing a sitz bath, it is very important to understand its contraindications and precautions, to ensure patient safety and prevent complications.

A sitz bath should be avoided, or performed only with caution, in patients with active or excessive bleeding from the perineal or rectal area, because warm water may increase circulation and worsen the bleeding.
Patients with severe infection, extensive tissue damage or deep wounds may require medical evaluation before the procedure, as improper technique can spread infection.
A sitz bath needs the patient's cooperation and their ability to communicate discomfort. Unconscious, confused or uncooperative patients are at higher risk of falls, burns and injury.
If any antiseptic or medicated solution is to be added to the water, check for allergies first, to avoid skin irritation, redness or an allergic reaction.

Patients with impaired sensation or neuropathy - diabetic patients in particular - may not feel excessive heat. These patients are at greater risk of burns and skin damage, so extra caution and careful temperature assessment are necessary.
And excessively hot water is itself a major risk. It causes burns, tissue injury and discomfort, so always check the water temperature before starting.

reveal.text: Type | What it does | Typically used for
reveal.cue_narration_line: Sitz baths are classified into three types, chosen by the patient's condition and the treatment goal.

reveal.text: Warm sitz bath | Improves circulation, relaxes muscles, reduces pain and swelling, promotes healing | Hemorrhoids, episiotomy wounds, anal fissure, postpartum discomfort. The most commonly used type
reveal.cue_narration_line: The warm sitz bath is the most commonly used. The patient sits in comfortably warm water for fifteen to twenty minutes - it improves circulation, relaxes muscles, reduces pain and swelling, and promotes healing.

reveal.text: Cold sitz bath | Causes vasoconstriction, reducing inflammation, swelling and local edema | Immediately after injury or surgery, for a short duration. Use carefully - excessive cold is uncomfortable
reveal.cue_narration_line: The cold sitz bath uses cool or cold water for a short duration, reducing inflammation and local edema by vasoconstriction. Use it carefully: excessive cold is uncomfortable for the patient.

reveal.text: Medicated sitz bath | Prescribed antiseptic or medicated solution reduces infection and cleanses the wound area | After rectal surgery or infection, and wounds needing special care. Only on medical advice
reveal.cue_narration_line: In the medicated sitz bath, a prescribed antiseptic or medicated solution is added to the water as advised by the doctor, to reduce infection and cleanse the wound area.

base_layer.reveal_note: one cue per line, synced to the narration line beside it
narration: Sitz baths are classified into three types, chosen by the patient's condition and the treatment goal.

The warm sitz bath is the most commonly used. The patient sits in comfortably warm water for fifteen to twenty minutes - it improves circulation, relaxes muscles, reduces pain and swelling, and promotes healing.
The cold sitz bath uses cool or cold water for a short duration, reducing inflammation and local edema by vasoconstriction. Use it carefully: excessive cold is uncomfortable for the patient.
In the medicated sitz bath, a prescribed antiseptic or medicated solution is added to the water as advised by the doctor, to reduce infection and cleanse the wound area.
The type follows the goal, and the goal comes from the doctor's order.

reveal.text: 40°C – 45°C — Recommended water temperature for a warm sitz bath
reveal.cue_narration_line: The recommended water temperature for a warm sitz bath is between forty and forty-five degrees Celsius. Water that is too hot causes burns and tissue damage; water that is too cold does not produce the therapeutic effect. Always check the temperature before starting.

reveal.text: 15 – 20 minutes — Long enough to improve circulation and relieve pain
reveal.cue_narration_line: The usual duration is about fifteen to twenty minutes. That is generally enough to improve blood circulation, relieve pain, reduce swelling and promote healing in the perineal area.

reveal.text: 2 – 3 times a day — Or as ordered by the physician
reveal.cue_narration_line: The frequency is usually two to three times a day, or as ordered by the physician depending on the patient's condition.

narration: Maintaining the correct water temperature is very important for patient comfort and safety.

The recommended water temperature for a warm sitz bath is between forty and forty-five degrees Celsius. Water that is too hot causes burns and tissue damage; water that is too cold does not produce the therapeutic effect. Always check the temperature before starting.
The usual duration is about fifteen to twenty minutes. That is generally enough to improve blood circulation, relieve pain, reduce swelling and promote healing in the perineal area.
The frequency is usually two to three times a day, or as ordered by the physician depending on the patient's condition.
Temperature, duration and frequency together are what make the therapy effective and safe.

narration: Proper preparation of the patient ensures comfort, safety, cooperation and an effective result. There are eight steps, and they run in this order.

interaction.build_as: slide layers on this slide, not separate slides

lines: Establish trust and a comfortable environment.
narration: Introduce yourself to the patient. Good communication establishes trust, reduces anxiety and improves cooperation during the procedure.

lines: Confirm name and PRN number against hospital policy.
narration: Identify the patient correctly by confirming their name and PRN or hospital identification number according to hospital policy. This ensures the right procedure is performed on the right patient.

lines: Purpose, duration and benefits, in simple language.
narration: Explain the procedure clearly in simple language and reassure the patient. Tell them the purpose, the duration and the expected benefits. This gains cooperation and reduces fear or embarrassment.

lines: Obtain consent if applicable. Close curtains or the door.
narration: Obtain the patient's consent if applicable, and provide privacy by closing the curtains or the door. Since the procedure involves the perineal area, dignity and privacy are extremely important.

lines: Before starting, to maintain aseptic practice.
narration: Perform hand hygiene before starting, to reduce the risk of infection and maintain aseptic practice.

lines: Check for circulatory impairment or skin problems where the bath will be applied.
narration: Assess the patient for any circulatory impairment, skin problems or contraindications in the area where the sitz bath or warm compress is to be applied. This prevents complications and keeps the patient safe.

lines: Type, duration, frequency and any prescribed solution.

slides.title: Complications, and how to prevent them

reveal.text: Complication | How it happens | How you prevent it
reveal.cue_narration_line: A sitz bath is generally safe, but complications can occur if precautions are not followed.

reveal.text: Burns | Water temperature too high | Check the temperature before every bath; never rely on the patient
reveal.cue_narration_line: Burns from hot water. If the temperature is too high it causes skin burns and tissue damage, so always check the temperature before the procedure.

reveal.text: Dizziness or fainting | Warmth and position change, usually getting in or out | Stay with the patient; assist in and out; support them while walking
reveal.cue_narration_line: Dizziness or fainting, especially while getting in or out of the basin. Continuous monitoring and assistance prevent falls and injury.

reveal.text: Infection | Poor hygiene or improperly cleaned equipment | Hand hygiene, clean equipment, follow infection control practice
reveal.cue_narration_line: Infection, from poor hygiene or improperly cleaned equipment. Cleanliness and infection control practice are essential.

reveal.text: Skin irritation | Excessive heat, prolonged soaking, or allergy to a solution | Keep to the prescribed temperature and duration; check allergies
reveal.cue_narration_line: Skin irritation, from excessive heat, prolonged soaking, or allergy to a medicated solution used in the bath.

reveal.text: Cross contamination | Equipment not cleaned between patients | Disinfect the basin after every use; hand hygiene throughout
reveal.cue_narration_line: And cross contamination, which happens when equipment is not cleaned between patients. Proper disinfection and hand hygiene prevent the spread of infection.

narration: Let us summarise the key points of the whole module.
A sitz bath is a warm water bath used to relieve discomfort in the perineal region and promote healing, by improving blood circulation and reducing pain, itching and irritation.
It is indicated for hemorrhoids, episiotomy wounds, postpartum perineal pain, anal fissures, rectal surgery and perianal abscesses.
Before performing it, assess for contraindications and precautions - active bleeding, severe infection, impaired sensation, allergy to medicated solutions, and the risk of burns from hot water.
There are warm, cold and medicated types, and a warm sitz bath runs at forty to forty-five degrees Celsius for fifteen to twenty minutes, two to three times a day.
Proper preparation of articles and patient, privacy, infection control and correct technique are essential for safe and effective care.

The benefits include improved circulation, reduced edema, muscle relaxation, pain relief, better hygiene and enhanced wound healing - while you stay alert for burns, dizziness, infection, skin irritation and cross contamination.
Your responsibilities run throughout: monitor comfort, check the water temperature, prevent falls, maintain infection control and educate the patient.
And accurate aftercare and documentation are what give the next nurse continuity of care.
By following these principles you can perform a sitz bath safely and effectively, and contribute significantly to patient comfort, healing and recovery.

Set the player per `player` — sidebar off, HOME and EXIT top right, bottom bar on.
Add the on-slide slide counter bound to the player variables.
Build each interaction as slide layers on its own slide, not as separate slides.
Give every layer its own audio and pause the base track when a layer opens.
Sync each base-layer reveal cue to the narration line beside it.
Build knowledge checks with three feedback layers over two attempts.
Source the images listed in `media` and replace the placeholder frames.
